issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (and instruct students to modify a Stock class and declare a 'final Stock stock' field), but the provided template and solution repositories contain a class named 'Inventory' that implements the expected stock behaviour. Additionally, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java in the template is empty. This naming mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) will confuse students: they will look for a Stock implementation to modify and for the Stock type to use in SealSaloon, but the concrete class available is Inventory. The inconsistency makes it unclear whether students should implement/modify Stock or use Inventory and may cause compilation/type confusion when following the problem text literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Rename Inventory.java (and the Inventory class) to Stock.java/Stock throughout the template and solution so it matches the problem statement and UML; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and clarify that the shared stock field is of type Inventory. Also remove or populate the empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java file in the template to avoid further confusion.
